# Welcome {.unnumbered .unlisted}

This is the online version of **Applied Generative AI for
Health Sciences Research** by The rgtlab Curriculum Project,
a graduate textbook for clinical and public-health research.

We cover the practical use of generative AI, large language
models, reasoning models, agents, and multimodal systems, in
clinical, public-health, and biostatistical research and
practice. The book is intended for graduate students and
working researchers, in clinical, public-health, and
biostatistical fields, who already know quantitative methods
at the level of a first-year graduate sequence. We assume the
reader is now adding AI assistance to that workflow and wants
to do so with appropriate discipline and verification.

The book sits alongside three companion volumes in the
series:

- [*Statistical Computing in the Age of AI*](https://scai.rgtlab.org),
  the introductory graduate computing volume.
- [*Advanced Statistical Computing in the Age of AI*](https://scai-advanced.rgtlab.org),
  the advanced computing volume covering numerical
  stability, optimization, Monte Carlo, and high-dimensional
  methods.
- [*Biostatistics Practicum*](https://practicum.rgtlab.org),
  the workflow companion covering Git, Docker, renv,
  Quarto, CDISC, and SAS.

We treat generative AI in this fourth volume as an
orthogonal axis. That is, it is not simply another method to
add to the curriculum. Rather, it is a collaborator to be
integrated into every stage of clinical and public-health
research, from exploratory analysis through deployment.

See the [Preface](preface.qmd) for motivation and the
[Conventions](conventions.qmd) page for visual cues used
throughout.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
The [Contents](contents.qmd) page lists every chapter on one page.
:::
